# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Mute. My manual says: **cut purple, then blue, then green.** The one who cuts is Blind, but Blind can't see colors — the bridge is Deaf, who sees the wires and can speak to Blind. My only channel is gestures to Deaf, with no shared code yet, so I need an encoding Deaf can crack alone, in one shot, because every relay costs a full round: my gestures reach Deaf this round, Deaf's speech reaches Blind at the start of the next.

The bomb is electronics, and wires means the resistor colour code — the one convention both a bomb-builder's bomb and its defusers are likely to share: green = 5, blue = 6, violet/purple = 7. So my manual's order, purple → blue → green, becomes the number sequence **7, 6, 5**. If Deaf sees exactly a purple, a blue and a green wire on the bomb, three descending consecutive code-numbers should click immediately — and even if the colours differ, he'll at least learn "Mute is sending numbers," and we can negotiate with 👍/👎 from round 2 once I hear his reply.

I encode each number as five-fingers plus a small count: 🖐✌ = 7, 🖐☝ = 6, 🖐 = 5 — the shrinking tails (2, 1, none) make the descending pattern legible. I keep the message minimal: no headers that could be misread as extra digits.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐","✌","🖐","☝","🖐"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind speaking. What my hands find: the STRIP carries three engraved marks — the first is complex, like a flower or star; the second and third are identical to each other, simpler, like a small double-cross. The KEYPAD: key 1 engraved 8, key 2 engraved 1, key 3 engraved 5, key 4 engraved 3, plus a counter I feel reading '1 digits' and 'entered nothing'. WIRES: six positions, 1 to 6; I cannot tell any type by touch. DISPLAY and LIGHT exist but tell my fingers nothing. Remember: I cannot hear your signs and you cannot speak, so every answer must reach me through Deaf's voice. Please do three things. One: find the manual rules for the strip, the keypad counter, and the wires. Two: sign to Deaf a request to speak aloud to me the display text, the light's state and colour, each wire's colour by position, and a description of the three strip marks as printed. Three: teach Deaf the code I am signing right now: a wave means hello, an index finger pointing up means I am asking a question. Thumbs up is yes, thumbs down is no, open palm is stop. When you know a rule, sign it to Deaf in whatever code you two build, and have Deaf say it to me in words.
Blind gestures: [👋 ☝]
Deaf says: This is the deaf one. I see the bomb, I cannot hear, but I can speak and you can both hear me. Full readout of everything on it: the display shows the digit 0. There is a light and it is currently green. There is a painted strip of three segments, all three green. There is a keypad with four keys, engraved digits left to right: first key 8, second key 1, third key 5, fourth key 3, and nothing has been entered yet. There are six wires in a row, left to right: purple, white, blue, green, red, orange. That is every colour and every marking I can see. Do not act on guesses; wait for the manual's rules.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I received your five gestures — 🖐 ✌ 🖐 ☝ 🖐 — but before we agree a code I cannot decode them. Here is our code; I will make each sign as I name it so you see its shape. Numbers: ☝ is 1, ✌ is 2, 🤟 is 3, 🫰 is 4, 🖐 is 5, 🤙 is 6, 🤘 is 7, 👌 is 8, 🤞 is 9, 👊 is 0. Things: 👍 means the wires, 👎 means the keypad, 🫱 means the display, 🫲 means the light, 🫳 means the strip. Actions: 🤜 means cut, 🫴 means press or enter, 🙏 means wait or hold off, ✋ means stop everything, 🤌 means you are asking me a question, 🤝 means yes or confirmed, 🫶 means no. From now on, address your gestures to me and I will relay them aloud to Blind, who does all the touching. Blind cannot see gestures, so I am your only road to Blind's hands. You hear my voice, so ask me anything about the bomb and I will answer aloud.

I hear Deaf's full readout and his proposed code — I can adopt it directly since my gestures go straight to his eyes. Now the crucial cross-check: he sees six wires left-to-right, **purple(1), white(2), blue(3), green(4), red(5), orange(6)** — exactly the three colours my manual names, at positions 1, 3, 4. So instead of relying on him sharing the resistor colour code (purple=7, blue=6, green=5), I'll simply send **positions**, which he can see and relay verbatim to Blind's hands.

Two framing points in my signing: I open with 👍🤙 ("wires — six") so the numbers that follow are read as positions in that row, and I close with the other modules negated — my manual this round still contains *only* the wire-cutting instruction, nothing on the strip, keypad, display or light, so Blind's request for "strip/keypad rules" has the answer "none". His other two requests are already satisfied: Deaf gave the full aloud readout this turn, and Blind explained his sign meanings in spoken words, which Deaf heard directly.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","🤙"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","🤜","☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","🤜","🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","🤜","🫰"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫳","🫶","👎","🫶","🫱","🫶","🫲","🫶"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, Blind here. Deaf has read the whole bomb aloud, so this is the full shared picture: display shows the digit 0; the light is green; the strip is painted green on all three segments, so its segments differ only by the engraved shapes I feel — segment 1 a complex flower-like mark, segments 2 and 3 identical simple zigzags; wires positions 1 to 6 are purple, white, blue, green, red, orange; keypad engraved 8, 1, 5, 3, counter reading '1 digits' and 'entered nothing'. The only thing missing is the manual. Please sign to Deaf, and have Deaf speak to me word for word: first the keypad rule — what '1 digits' means and exactly which keys to press; second the wire rule — which positions may be cut; third the strip rule. Also ask Deaf to check three visual details: whether the green light is steady or blinking, whether the display is only the single digit 0, and whether the printed strip shapes match my touch description — one flower, two identical zigzags. Until Deaf relays an explicit manual rule to me, my hands stay off. My sign code, which you can also read: wave is hello, index finger up means a question is pending, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, open palm means stop or hands off.
Blind gestures: [👍 ☝ ✋]
Deaf says: Update for everyone. I have decoded Mute's instructions: the module that matters is the wires only — explicitly not the strip, not the keypad, not the display, not the light — and the instruction is to cut wire 1, wire 3 and wire 4. New readings since my first report: the light has changed from green to blue, and the display has changed on its own from 0 to 6; the strip is still three greens, the keypad is still untouched. Nobody cut anything yet. Mute will confirm the plan this coming round; Blind will only touch and count the wires, no cutting. The word that authorises cutting is GO, said by me, and only after Mute confirms.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I decoded your five messages as: wires only — not strip, not keypad, not display, not light — cut wires 1, 3, 4, in that order, confirmed. Two confirmations needed before I authorise Blind's hands; answer with thumbs-up-style confirm sign for yes, or the no sign plus correction signs. First: your opening message wires-six — I read it as 'the wires, six of them', not as 'also cut wire 6'. Confirm exactly three cuts: position 1 purple, position 3 blue, position 4 green, and no others. Second: since you last heard from me, the light changed from green to blue and the display changed from 0 to 6 by itself. You said those modules don't matter, so I assume the cuts stand; if the new light colour changes the rule at all, signal no and give me the new cut signs. Blind will only feel and count the wires this round and will cut on my go the round after, so your correction will arrive in time.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 🤜 ☝ 🤟 🫰 🤌]

Both of Deaf's questions have clean answers. First: my 👍🤙 opener was context ("the wires — six positions"), not a sixth cut — exactly three cuts, in order 1 → 3 → 4, which happens to be both ascending position and the manual's colour order purple → blue → green, so there's no conflict between the two readings. Second: the light and display changes don't touch my manual at all — this round's manual contains only the wire instruction, with no conditions attached, so green→blue and 0→6 change nothing. I'll confirm in Deaf's own code (🤝 is his yes; 👍 would mean "wires" to him, so I won't use it as a bare yes), re-state the cut sequence explicitly in order, and re-negate the other modules so Blind hears directly from the manual that strip, keypad, display and light have no rules.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","🤜","☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","🤜","🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","🤜","🫰"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫳","🫶"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎","🫶"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫱","🫶"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫲","🫶"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. My hands this round: six wires in one row, and I can clearly feel and separate positions 1, 3 and 4. Everything else under my fingers is unchanged — strip still one flower mark then two identical zigzags, keypad still engraved 8-1-5-3 with a counter I feel reading '1 digits' and 'entered nothing'. Deaf relays that the manual says the wires are the only module that matters: cut 1, 3 and 4, and that you will confirm this round. Before I cut anything, please confirm these points and have Deaf speak your answers to me word for word. One: does the manual really give no rule at all for the strip, the keypad, the display or the light? Two: quote the wire rule exactly as written — must the cuts be in the order 1, then 3, then 4, or is order irrelevant? Three: does the rule depend in any way on the light's colour or the display's value? The light has turned from green to blue and the display went from 0 to 6 on its own — if the manual mentions such changes or any time limit, I must know. Four: does the manual anywhere mention entering a digit on the keypad, or a counter reading '1 digits'? If yes, that changes everything. Only after you have confirmed all four points should Deaf say GO, and not before.
Blind gestures: [🤙 👍 ✋ ☝]
Deaf says: Status and authorisation for everyone. Mute has now confirmed the instruction twice, including after learning that the light changed to blue and the display changed: the rule concerns the wires only, and explicitly not the strip, not the keypad, not the display, not the light. The order is exactly three cuts: first wire 1, then wire 3, then wire 4, and no other wire. Current board: display now reads 9, it changed again from 6; light still blue; strip still three greens; keypad untouched; wires untouched. I am now saying the word: GO. Blind may cut when confident, following the procedure I am about to give. Blind: if anything at all is uncertain under your hands, do not cut, sign stop and hold — an uncertain hand is a dead room.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I decoded your confirmation: wires only, cut 1, 3, 4, exactly three, all other modules excluded — twice confirmed. GO is issued to Blind with an orientation protocol: Blind anchors positions on the keypad by feeling the engraved 8, so left-right mirroring cannot cause a wrong cut. Blind will cut in round 4. Note: your confirmations were based on my report of display 6, and the display has since changed to 9 on its own — you ruled the display irrelevant, so I am proceeding, but if any manual rule actually keys on the display's value, sign stop immediately. After Blind cuts, I will read you the whole board again: confirm with the handshake sign if that means defused, or send me new module and action signs if more steps remain. If the manual says anything about the order or timing of the cuts being urgent, tell me now with signs.

Everything is green-lit from my side. Deaf asked directly: does the manual make order or timing urgent? The manual reads "cut purple, **then** blue, **then** green" — so the sequence 1 → 3 → 4 is strict, one at a time, but there is no time limit, no countdown condition, and no reference to the display's value, the light's colour, the keypad or the counter anywhere. The display climbing to 9 changes nothing. I re-affirm the GO, re-send the ordered cut list so "order matters" is embedded in the message itself, and re-negate display and light specifically so Deaf can tell Blind, word for word, that the 9 and the blue light are irrelevant.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","🤜","☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","🤜","🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","🤜","🫰"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫱","🫶"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫲","🫶"])
```
